requirements.title: Namelist formatting uses the editing rules of 13.11
requirements.definition: If namelist formatting has been established, editing is performed as described in 13.11.

pending.namelist-formatting-edited-by-13-11: Future fixtures first establish NML= under 12.6.4.4, initialize namelist variables to nondefault sentinels, and assert only Clause 13.11 namelist properties.

requirements.oracle: Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans establish a non-default state first (for example by opening or creating a known file, writing known records, initializing variables to nonzero/nonblank sentinels, or using a distinct labelled control path) and then observe only portable properties: successful IOSTAT zero, nonzero IOSTAT for a specified error condition, exact internal records or values where the source fixes them, named ISO_FORTRAN_ENV status values where the standard names them, or INQUIRE properties fixed by the relevant rule. Processor-dependent unit numbers, filenames except names created by the fixture, storage-unit encodings, buffering, asynchronous timing, IOMSG text, and specific numeric status values are not asserted.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Source accounting only. This packet creates no Fortran fixture, compiler invocation, execution evidence, evidence link, fixture approval, oracle approval, or coverage claim. Negative plans are source-control plans unless this unit itself requires rejection and a future fixture can observe that rejection portably; unnumbered program restrictions are not promoted to required diagnostics. IOMSG wording, processor-dependent numeric status values, asynchronous completion timing, and multiple-image or coarray-dependent behavior are never single-image oracles; coarray facets remain out of scope for this suite's fixtures.
requirements.dependencies: Registered dependencies: clauses 6, 8, 9, 10, and 11 for source form, names, expressions, execution constructs, and existing declaration/execution foundations; registered earlier clause 12 catalogues for file existence, access, file position, internal files, connection, data-transfer statements, and control-list forms where present. Unregistered dependencies explicitly retained: 12.6.2.2/12.6.3 sibling source packets, later 12.6.4.8 defined I/O, clause 13 formatting, clause 15 defined I/O procedure accessibility, clause 16 inquiry and ISO_FORTRAN_ENV intrinsics where future fixtures need them, clause 14 image semantics only as out-of-scope context, and clauses 3, 5, 17, 18, and 19 where terminology, IEEE support, deleted features, or program execution controls are reached.

requirements.title: Namelist objects must be ready for transfer or use defined I/O for dynamic/allocatable-pointer structure
requirements.definition: Every allocatable namelist-group-object shall be allocated, every pointer namelist-group-object shall be associated with a target, and polymorphic objects or objects with ultimate allocatable or pointer components shall be processed by a defined input/output procedure.

pending.namelist-allocatable-objects-allocated: Positive control allocates an allocatable namelist object and assigns a nondefault value before namelist transfer; source-control negative leaves it unallocated with no required diagnostic claim.
pending.namelist-pointer-objects-associated: Positive control associates a pointer namelist object with a target initialized to a distinct value before transfer; source-control negative leaves it disassociated.
pending.namelist-polymorphic-processed-by-define: After 12.6.4.8 registration, provide a defined I/O procedure that writes/reads a visible token for a polymorphic namelist object; without defined I/O no portable single-image fixture is claimed.
pending.namelist-ultimate-alloc-pointer-componen: After defined I/O registration, use a derived type with an ultimate allocatable or pointer component and a defined I/O procedure that transfers a sentinel-distinct value; coarray/image-dependent variants remain out of scope.

review_rationale: Source registration for 12.6.4-12.6.4.7, execution of a data transfer statement (batch162). Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer across two rounds. Round 1 found that the '*', INPUT_UNIT and OUTPUT_UNIT equality facets were planned through stdin/stdout capture and separate controls, which cannot observe unit identity; they are now recorded as having no portable oracle because 12.5.4 makes connecting one file to several units, and I/O through them, processor dependent, and neither NAME= nor NUMBER= rescues it. Source accounting only.
